episode.title: Adapt model selection, metadata, and requests to an alternate OpenAI-compatible provider endpoint
episode.before: At parent bcf4a557141a70fdb8e80d15c565ffaa654b44b9, one Model implementation recognized only GPT-style names, derived context limits and pricing from hard-coded rules, and rejected unsupported names. Model instances were constructed before the configured API endpoint was applied. Tokenizers and helper-model names were also selected directly at several consumers, while chat requests had no provider-specific attribution headers.
episode.after: At 30a3cc08470ac71878029c77775b4e9706b2c378, model creation occurs after API endpoint configuration and dispatches through a provider-aware factory. The alternate-provider adapter normalizes familiar aliases, selects editing behavior, uses a fallback tokenizer, queries the provider model catalog for context length and pricing, and rejects absent models. Consumers use model-owned tokenizer and helper-model properties, and requests to the alternate endpoint include its required attribution headers.
episode.diff: The merge replaces the monolithic model module with a common model interface plus provider-specific implementations; changes startup to use Model.create after endpoint configuration; propagates model objects and their tokenizer through summarization, commands, repository mapping, and commit-message generation; adds alternate-endpoint request headers; guards a response field that may be absent; and extends model tests with a mocked provider catalog asserting alias normalization, context length, and price conversion.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 30a3cc08470ac71878029c77775b4e9706b2c378 is the merge of pull request #199, titled “Openrouter compatibility,” with first parent bcf4a557141a70fdb8e80d15c565ffaa654b44b9.
Before the change, aider/models.py contained one Model constructor that inferred context size and pricing from GPT name patterns and raised ValueError for unsupported model families.
Startup now applies openai API endpoint settings before invoking Model.create(args.model), allowing endpoint configuration to participate in adapter selection.

Model.create selects the alternate-provider adapter when openai.api_base contains openrouter.ai and otherwise selects the standard adapter; helper methods create strong, weak, and commit-message model objects through the same factory.

The alternate-provider adapter maps three familiar GPT aliases to provider-qualified identifiers, derives edit format and repository-map behavior, and supplies a cl100k_base tokenizer pending model-specific encodings.

The alternate-provider adapter caches the provider model catalog, finds the requested identifier, imports context length and per-token prices into the local model contract, and raises ValueError when the model is absent.
Commands and repository-map construction now consume main_model.tokenizer instead of independently asking tiktoken to resolve an encoding from the model name.
Chat summarization now stores a weak model object, uses its tokenizer, and sends with its resolved name; coder construction supplies the provider-aware weak model.
Commit-message generation obtains provider-aware model objects from Model.commit_message_models and passes their resolved names to the chat request function.
Chat requests whose configured API base targets the alternate provider receive HTTP-Referer and X-Title headers, while other endpoint requests retain the prior request shape.
Streaming response handling checks that finish_reason exists before comparing it with length, accommodating provider responses that omit that attribute.

The model tests preserve context-window assertions for standard models through Model.create and add a mocked alternate-provider catalog test covering alias qualification, context length, and prompt/completion price conversion.
An attempted isolated execution of python3 -m unittest tests.test_models at the pinned commit did not reach the tests because the environment lacked the tiktoken dependency.
evidence_units.source: local validation command in detached worktree at 30a3cc08470ac71878029c77775b4e9706b2c378; ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tiktoken'

evidence_units.claim: The first-parent diff changes model construction, model metadata resolution, tokenizer ownership, helper-model call sites, request headers, response compatibility, documentation, and tests across the files recorded in the issue bundle.

candidate_atomics.name: select-model-adapter-after-endpoint-configuration
candidate_atomics.description: Resolve a model through an endpoint-aware factory only after runtime provider settings have been installed.

semantic_action.intent: Select the model implementation whose behavior matches the configured API endpoint.
semantic_action.pre_state: Model construction used one provider-specific implementation and occurred before endpoint configuration could influence selection.
semantic_action.post_state: Each requested model is constructed by the adapter selected from the active endpoint configuration.
semantic_action.validation: Standard context-window tests exercise the default factory route; the alternate adapter is directly exercised with a mocked provider catalog.

candidate_atomics.name: normalize-provider-model-metadata
candidate_atomics.description: Translate aliases and remote catalog data into the application's common model capabilities and accounting fields.

semantic_action.intent: Make provider-hosted models satisfy the local model contract without hard-coding their context limits and prices.
semantic_action.pre_state: The local model constructor recognized only GPT-style names and derived metadata from fixed name and pricing rules.
semantic_action.post_state: A provider-qualified model has an edit format, tokenizer, context limit, and normalized pricing populated from provider-aware rules and catalog data, or fails explicitly when absent.
semantic_action.validation: The mocked catalog test asserts alias qualification, an 8192-token context, and conversion of provider prices to 0.06 and 0.12 per thousand tokens.

candidate_atomics.name: propagate-model-owned-capabilities-to-consumers
candidate_atomics.description: Have token-counting and helper-model consumers use resolved model objects rather than reconstructing provider assumptions from names.

semantic_action.intent: Keep downstream behavior consistent with the selected provider adapter.
semantic_action.pre_state: Consumers independently selected tokenizers or used fixed helper-model names, bypassing provider-specific resolution.
semantic_action.post_state: Consumers receive model objects, use model-owned tokenizers, and send requests using provider-resolved model names.
semantic_action.validation: Diff inspection shows the command, repository-map, summary, coder, and commit-message call sites all changed to consume the shared model abstraction.

candidate_atomics.name: augment-provider-compatible-chat-requests
candidate_atomics.description: Conditionally attach endpoint-specific attribution metadata while preserving the common chat-completion call.

semantic_action.intent: Meet an alternate provider endpoint's request-interface expectations through the existing chat transport.
semantic_action.pre_state: All chat-completion requests used the same payload and supplied no alternate-provider attribution headers.
semantic_action.post_state: Requests targeting the alternate endpoint include HTTP-Referer and X-Title headers; requests to other endpoints remain unchanged.
semantic_action.validation: Implementation inspection verifies the endpoint-guarded headers branch; no direct request-header test is present in the pinned change.

candidate_atomics.name: guard-optional-provider-response-field
candidate_atomics.description: Check for an optional response attribute before applying the existing context-exhaustion rule.

semantic_action.intent: Avoid failing when a compatible provider omits a response field used by the default provider.
semantic_action.post_state: A missing finish_reason does not raise an attribute-access error, while an available value of length still signals context exhaustion.
semantic_action.validation: The first-parent diff directly shows the hasattr guard; no focused test for the omitted-field response shape is included.

candidate_workflows.name: adapt-an-openai-compatible-provider-endpoint
candidate_workflows.description: Introduce an endpoint-selected model adapter, carry its capabilities through consumers, and isolate provider-specific request and response differences at transport boundaries.

workflow_graph.goal: Allow models exposed through a compatible alternate endpoint to participate in existing editing, token accounting, summarization, repository mapping, commit-message, and chat workflows.
workflow_graph.entry_state: The application has a single-provider model implementation, provider assumptions are duplicated at consumers, and the compatible endpoint has metadata and wire-level differences.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Endpoint configuration selects the appropriate adapter; resolved model capabilities flow to consumers; provider-specific request and response differences are bounded at transport interfaces; standard model behavior remains covered by tests.
unresolved_or_deferred: No direct test in the pinned change verifies conditional request headers.
No direct test in the pinned change verifies handling of a response choice without finish_reason.
The complete test result is unavailable because the local validation environment lacks tiktoken.
The provider catalog cache has process-global scope and its invalidation behavior is not tested.
Provider-specific tokenizer accuracy for non-OpenAI models is explicitly left as a TODO in the implementation.

unresolved_questions: Would the full historical dependency environment pass tests/test_models.py and broader integration tests at the pinned commit?
Should endpoint detection use parsed host equality instead of substring matching in openai.api_base?
How should provider catalog caching behave if credentials, endpoint, or available models change during a process?
Which provider-hosted model families require model-specific tokenizers or editing formats beyond the fallback heuristics?
